design.text: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, two-arm parallel trial; subjects randomized 2:1 to acoramidis 712 mg (800 mg acoramidis HCl) twice daily or matching placebo, followed for 30 months.

endpoint.text: Primary endpoint: a hierarchical combination of all-cause mortality (ACM), cumulative frequency of CV-related hospitalizations (CVH), change from baseline in NT-proBNP, and change from baseline in 6MWD over the 30-month trial duration.

citations.quote: A hierarchical combination of all-cause mortality (ACM), cumulative frequency of cardiovascular-related hospitalizations (CVH) as adjudicated by the CEC, CFB in NTproBNP, and CFB in the distance walked during 6MWT over the 30-month double-blind trial duration.

n.text: 632 randomized (421 acoramidis, 211 placebo); mITT efficacy population N=611.

citations.quote: Trial AG10-301 was a 2-arm, double-blind, parallel design trial with 632 subjects randomized in a 2:1 ratio to acoramidis 712 mg twice daily (equivalent to 800 mg acoramidis HCl) or matching placebo (421 to acoramidis and 211 to placebo) and followed for 30 months at which time all randomized subjects were eligible to enroll in the OLE trial (AG10-304).

The efficacy analyses were conducted in the mITT population (N=611), which included randomized participants with eGFR >30 mL/min/1.73 m2. The safety analysis was conducted in the safety population (N=632) (Table 12).

result.text: Primary endpoint met: Win ratio 1.77 (96% CI 1.40, 2.24), p<0.0001; at 30 months 81% alive on acoramidis versus 74% on placebo and fewer CVH events (0.3 versus 0.6 per year).

citations.quote: Primary analysis: The result of primary endpoint analysis demonstrated a statistically significant reduction in ACM and cumulative frequency of CVH, difference in CFB in NT-proBNP (\ge 500 pg/mL), and difference in CFB in 6MWT in the acoramidis group versus the placebo group (Win ratio [96% CI]: 1.77 [1.40, 2.24], p<0.0001). At 30 months, more subjects were alive on acoramidis treatment versus the placebo group (81% versus 74%) and there were fewer CVH events (0.3 versus 0.6 per year) (Table 15 and Table 16). The first three components (ACM, CVH and NT-proBNP) seemed to contribute evenly to the overall result, ~29% (Table 17).

indication.text: ATTRUBY is a transthyretin stabilizer indicated for the treatment of the cardiomyopathy of wild-type or variant transthyretin-mediated amyloidosis (ATTR-CM) in adults to reduce cardiovascular death and cardiovascular-related hospitalization.

target_moa.text: Acoramidis is a selective stabilizer of transthyretin (TTR); it binds TTR at thyroxine binding sites and slows dissociation of the TTR tetramer into its constituent monomers, the rate-limiting step in amyloidogenesis.

citations.quote: Acoramidis is a selective stabilizer of transthyretin (TTR). Acoramidis binds TTR at thyroxine binding sites and slows dissociation of the TTR tetramer into its constituent monomers, the rate-limiting step in amyloidogenesis.
Acoramidis (AG10) is a small molecule that binds to and stabilizes tetrameric TTR protein, preventing its dissociation.

key_safety.text: Higher frequency of gastrointestinal adverse reactions with ATTRUBY: diarrhea 11.6% vs 7.6% and upper abdominal pain 5.5% vs 1.4% versus placebo; most were mild. Discontinuation due to an adverse event was similar (9.3% vs 8.5%).

citations.quote: There was a higher frequency of gastrointestinal (GI) adverse reactions such as diarrhea 11.6% versus 7.6% and upper abdominal pain 5.5% versus 1.4% in the ATTRUBY versus placebo group, respectively. The majority of these GI adverse reactions were categorized as mild and resolved without drug discontinuation.
A similar proportion of ATTRUBY-treated and placebo-treated participants discontinued study drug because of an adverse event (9.3% and 8.5%, respectively).
